circuits.issue: The 32 A MCB and lack of RCD protection are correct, but the drawn cable is 2.5 mm²; the specification requires a minimum 6 mm² copper cable.
The 40 A MCB and 10 mm² cable are correct, but the shower circuit is not shown with the required 30 mA RCD protection.

sequence.action: Identify the installation and all sources of supply, switch off the 63 A main switch, isolate and lock off, display warning notices, and prove the voltage tester before and after proving the installation dead.

Inspect the drawing and installation points, confirm the earthing arrangement and main earthing terminal, identify all six final circuits, and verify that the planned protective devices and cable routes match the specification.
Install the six final circuits as designed, retaining the 20 A MCBs and 2.5 mm² cables for C1 and C2, the 6 A MCBs and 1.5 mm² cables for C3 and C4, and the 40 A MCB and 10 mm² cable for C6.

Correct the non-compliant circuits before energizing: install a minimum 6 mm² copper cable for C5 and provide 30 mA RCD protection for C6. Confirm that C1 and C2 remain supplied through the drawn 30 mA RCD.
Test continuity of protective conductors for C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, and C6, including CPCs to all relevant accessories and exposed-conductive-parts, and record the results.

Carry out insulation resistance tests for C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, and C6 between the relevant live conductors and between live conductors and earth, protecting or disconnecting sensitive equipment as necessary.
Verify polarity for C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, and C6 at the origin and final accessories, confirming correct line, neutral, and protective-conductor connections.
After satisfactory dead tests and completion of the inspection, remove temporary earths and tools, refit covers, and re-energize the installation under controlled conditions.
Measure earth fault loop impedance for C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, and C6 at the relevant furthest points and confirm that the results permit the protective devices to disconnect within the required limits.

Test RCD operation for the RCD protecting C1 and C2, and test the installed 30 mA RCD protecting C6. Carry out the required RCD operation verification for C3, C4, and C5 in accordance with the project test schedule and record the applicable protective arrangement.
Carry out functional tests on every circuit: socket outlets C1 and C2, lighting circuits C3 and C4, cooker C5, and bathroom shower C6, confirming correct operation and safe isolation controls.

Review all inspection and test results, rectify any failures, label the consumer unit and circuits, provide the test and verification records, explain the installation and isolation arrangements to the client, and hand over the completed installation.
